answer: Because the ferrous index resolves every citation against the whisper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the orchard audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 230 aliases as a result burns the authoring cost 230 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 2840 identities would post 3110 proofs and burn roughly 37 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
